title.narrative: WASH in Emergency Early Lifesaving Response to Communities Projected to be Most Affected by El Nino-induced Riverine Flooding in Baardheere, District of Gedo region.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif font-size: 8pt text-align: justify"gtThe humanitarian crisis in Somalia is worsening, with over 8 million people in need of urgent assistance. The expected El Niño and positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) are expected to result in above-average rainfall for the upcoming Deyr rains, October-December, which could lead to severe flooding, loss of life, livelihoods, and property, population displacement, and destruction of infrastructure and crops. lt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="text-align:justify"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-size:8.0ptmso-bidi-font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gtThe anticipated El Niño and positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) are expected to result in above-average rainfall for the upcoming Deyr rains, October-December, which could lead to severe flooding, loss of life, livelihoods, and property, population displacement, and destruction of infrastructure and crops. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="text-align:justify"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-size:8.0ptmso-bidi-font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gtTo mitigate the impact of the floods and prevent waterborne diseases, the project will focus on providing water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services to 25,000 people, including communities affected by floods and at risk of cholera outbreaks, displaced people with no access to basic sanitation facilities, and school and healthcare facility users in Bardhere District of Gedo region. lt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="text-align:justify"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-size:8.0ptmso-bidi-font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gt lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
ltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtHIRDA will therefore respond to these augmented risks and crises through the provision of life-saving WASH intervention in Bardera in Gedo region of Somalia. Through this intervention, HIRDA will target a total of 4,167 households (25,000 individuals) in Bardera district. In order to create synergies and ensure sequencing, layering and integrating of programming, HIRDA will complement the proposed intervention with an ongoing Joint Resilience program of Nutrition, Education, and WASH in public institutions in the targeted areas and will work closely with other WASH cluster partners, CCM cluster. HIRDA will rehabilitate three (3) strategic shallow wells. conduct routine chlorination of 15 community water sources, conduct routine water quality testing such as the FRC test, and establish and train 3 gender balance water management committees to manage water sources rehabilitate, This water infrastructure will be constructed through community, local authority, line ministries and gender-balanced water management committees to ensure operation and maintenance. In addition to that HIRDA will provide emergency water trucking to 10,000 beneficiaries for two months. HIRDA proposed to construct 120 disaster, disability gender sensitive emergency latrines IDPs. construction of 6 group handwashing facilities for public institutions. This will be accompanied by solid waste management campaigns and 600 households that will benefit from latrine construction will be provided with portable solar lamps, purchase and distribution of 80 sanitation tool kits to sanitation groups and this will be accompanied by 24 clean-up campaigns during the project durations. HIRDA purchase and distribute 1,500 hygiene kits and massive hygiene promotion activities including but not limited to 24 hygiene promotion sessions and hygiene promoters training on AWD/cholera prevention. The full suite of activities aims to meet both the acute and long-term needs of the vulnerable IDP communities, whilst establishing relationships with the target communities for continued maintenance and operation of these assets. HIRDA WASH technical designs adhere to SPHERE standards/Somalia WASH cluster guidelines, mainstreaming protection and disability, and gender considerations per IASC guidelines for GBV Interventions in Humanitarian settings. HIRDA will ensure community participation and inclusion in all project implementation processes. HIRDA will promote women's participation in project activities including WASH infrastructure like water facilities.lt/spangt
